summary_hint: SSA <benefit_type> award for <beneficiary_name> (claim <claim_number_masked>), letter dated <award_or_benefit_verification_letter_date>: gross <gross_monthly_benefit>/mo, net <net_monthly_payment>/mo; continuance <benefit_end_or_review_date>.

typed_core.name: beneficiary_name
typed_core.why: identity — whose income; match to the borrower

typed_core.name: claim_number_masked
typed_core.why: PII (highly_restricted) + identity — the SSA claim key
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the claim-number suffix (A=wage earner, B=spouse, C=child, D=widow(er)) — it signals continuance risk (child benefits end)

typed_core.name: benefit_type
typed_core.why: IN-13 — the income type detection (retirement / SSDI / SSI / survivors); determines usability and continuance
typed_core.prompt_hint: SSI (needs-based) and SSDI (disability) differ from retirement in usability and continuance under IN-13

typed_core.name: award_or_benefit_verification_letter_date
typed_core.why: IN-13 — recency of the award/verification evidence

typed_core.name: net_monthly_payment
typed_core.why: processor — matches to the bank-deposit proof of receipt
typed_core.prompt_hint: Net monthly payment = gross − Medicare/other deductions; the deposit on bank statements matches the net

typed_core.name: payment_schedule_or_day
typed_core.why: processor — receipt-matching (which day of month deposits land)

typed_core.name: benefit_end_or_review_date
typed_core.why: IN-13 — the continuance test (3-year likelihood; a review/end date within the window flags)

typed_core.name: continuation_or_age_dependency_terms
typed_core.why: IN-13 — continuance terms (e.g. child/survivor benefits ending at a dependent's age)

nested_lists.name: medicare_or_other_deductions
nested_lists.shape_reason: reconciles gross → net; genuinely repeats (Medicare Part B, Part D, tax withholding) but is small (≤~4 items), so flat rows are cheap

fields.name: label
fields.why: IN-13 — the deduction label (Medicare Part B/D, tax withholding)

fields.name: amount
fields.why: IN-13 — the deduction amount; reconciles gross → net

fields.name: source
fields.why: provenance — the row the value came from

rejected.name: form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: an SSA award letter is not a standardized filled form

rejected.name: document_issue_date, effective_date, expiration_date
rejected.reason: duplicate the letter date / entitlement date

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: SSA letters are agency-issued, not executed/notarized

rejected.name: ssa_contact_or_verification_reference
rejected.reason: contact/reference only; no rule or processor gate; catch-all

encoding_variations: benefit_type — 'Retirement', 'Disability (SSDI)', 'Supplemental Security Income (SSI)', 'Survivors'; SSI is need-based and may not be usable/continuing — a critical IN-13 distinction; degrade enum to str

claim-number suffix — the letters after the SSN-based claim number (A = wage earner, B = spouse, C = child, D = widow(er)) signal continuance risk (child benefits end); capture verbatim as the continuance disambiguator
gross vs net — 'Monthly benefit amount' (gross) vs 'amount you receive' (net after Medicare); keep both
award vs verification letter — an original award letter vs an annual Benefit Verification / COLA letter; award_or_benefit_verification_letter_date covers both

open_questions.q: Deductions as a nested list vs catch-all — medicare_or_other_deductions is small and only supports gross→net reconciliation
options: drop it to the catch-all and keep only gross/net scalars
open_questions.recommendation: (b) drop to catch-all unless a rule needs itemized deductions

options: leave benefit_end_or_review_date + continuation_or_age_dependency_terms for the rule to interpret
open_questions.recommendation: (a) leave the fields for the rule; months-to-end is a conclusion, not a fact

open_questions.q: SSI usability — SSI may be non-continuing/non-qualifying
open_questions.recommendation: confirm whether benefit_type alone suffices for IN-13 or a separate program-eligibility flag is wanted

notes: A 'Benefit Verification Letter' (a.k.a. 'budget letter', 'proof of income letter') is the common re-issued form; treat it as the same document type.
claim_number_masked is registered pre_masked true — the SSA claim number is SSN-derived; beneficiary_name / representative_payee are standard-sensitivity names, not registry PII.
Ambiguity: representative_payee is tagged 'processor/identity' — classed processor as primary (a payee ≠ beneficiary flag); flagged.
